headline: India eagerly awaits Tarique Rahman's visit to Delhi
summary: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi says PM Narendra Modi believes a visit could help resolve bilateral issues between the two nations.
details: Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, stated that India is still eagerly awaiting a visit to Delhi by Tarique Rahman.

Speaking at an event for an Indian business delegation in Dhaka, Trivedi mentioned that Prime Minister Narendra Modi believes such a visit would enable both countries to work toward resolving any existing issues.
The High Commissioner emphasized that the Indian government has extended an invitation to Tarique Rahman, describing him as a 'people's prime minister' and expressing optimism about the visit.
Regarding bilateral relations, Trivedi noted that while the current administration in Bangladesh is working under the 'Bangladesh First' slogan, India shares a similar policy of mutual respect.
He added that while it is not necessary to forget the past, there is a significant opportunity to focus on a new future together.
Trivedi stressed that advancing the relationship between the two nations requires mutual and selfless trust, and that any problems can be solved through dialogue.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shama Oubaed Islam, also spoke at the event, stating that Bangladesh seeks effective steps to resolve pending issues regarding the Prime Minister's visit.
She further emphasized that Bangladesh desires an economic partnership where both nations benefit equally.

headline: Man beaten to death over child-lifting suspicion in Khulna
summary: A 26-year-old man was lynched by a mob in the Rayermohol area of Khulna city after being suspected of child-lifting.
details: A 26-year-old man named Raju Shikdar was beaten to death by a mob in the Rayermohol area of Khulna city on Tuesday afternoon.
The incident occurred near the big mosque of Rayermohol market in the Arongghata police station area. Raju was seen with a child, which sparked suspicion among locals.
A group of people detained him and began beating him while questioning him on suspicion of child-lifting. More people joined in, and the assault continued.
Police responded to a 999 emergency call and rescued Raju from the mob, finding him in critical condition.
He was rushed to Khulna Medical College Hospital, where he died during treatment on Tuesday evening around 6:30 PM.
Assistant Commissioner of Police (Sonadanga Zone) Humayun Kabir stated that police are investigating whether the child with Raju was known to him.
The police have launched an investigation to uncover the actual cause of the incident and have vowed to take legal action against those involved in the lynching.
